correctness.rationale: On the unfilled tree a descending link is a discrete set and has a cone vertex exactly when an earlier neighbor is unique. Without a center-matched incidence, each arm supports only a subset of {A_i,C_i} or the isolated B_i; the maximal choices are realizable by processing B-arms before c and other arms after c. An order for a one-B choice also matches c, which causes no problem for downward closure. If D_i matches c, all other u_j come after c, excluding B_j; both advertised extensions with D_i are attained by explicit orders. Its link is coned by A_j for any j≠i. After removing all D_i, each C_i is dominated by A_i. The remaining join is the boundary of the n-cross-polytope. Its equivariant inclusion is a homology isomorphism, and permuting degree-zero join factors of the fundamental cycle contributes the sign of the arm permutation, without requiring equivariance of the deletion order. Of the 2^n join facets, exactly n one-B facets extend to a D-facet; adding the 2n D-facets gives 2^n+n. The all-B and all-A,C facets have distinct dimensions for n≥3. An independent full vertex-order enumeration and link check through n=4 corroborate the proof.
residual_risks: Finite replay covers n≤4; the exact decomposition proves the unbounded claim. The boundary case n=2 is not credited as new.
